title: Sep 17 Results + Sep 18 Preview: Model Found Its Rhythm in the Middle Innings
summary: 5-4 day with strong favorites hitting. Tomorrow we're backing Burns in Cincy.

content.value:
## Sep 17: Solid Contact, Mixed Results

From a pitcher's perspective, yesterday was like working through a lineup the second time around—you figure some things out. We went 5-4 with a 55.6% hit rate, and honestly, that's the kind of day where the process matters more than perfection. The higher-confidence picks came through when we needed them.

## What Worked on the Mound

Our three 61%+ confidence plays all cashed. That's execution when it counts—like throwing your fastball in a hitter's count and getting the swing-and-miss. The Astros, Padres, and Rays picks showed why trusting your best stuff pays off. The Angels pick at 61% was the fifth winner, giving us solid depth beyond the top tier.

## The Misses: Coin Flips Don't Always Land Your Way

All four losses came on picks between 50-52% confidence. That's essentially pitcher's duel territory—could go either way. The Mets, Reds, Tigers, and Brewers didn't come through, but when you're picking games that tight, you expect some variance. No pitcher wins every 3-2 count.

## Sep 18 Preview: Eyes on Great American Ball Park

Tomorrow's top pick brings us to Cincinnati where the Reds host the Cubs. From the mound, this matchup is interesting—Clay Holmes making the start for Chicago against Chase Burns for the home squad.

content.title: ⭐ Tomorrow's Top Pick - Sep 18
content.sub: 50% confidence · Burns vs Holmes · Great American Ball Park

content.value:
## The Pitching Matchup

Holmes transitioning to starter duty for the Cubs faces Burns, who's got home cooking at Great American. This is a 50% confidence call, which tells me it's another tight one. But there's value in backing the home arm who knows his ballpark. Burns has the advantage of familiarity—he knows how the ball carries in Cincinnati, where the wind's coming from, and how to work that short porch in right.

Holmes has been solid, but starting versus relieving is a different animal. You're facing the lineup multiple times, can't just air it out for one inning. That adjustment factor gives me enough to lean Reds.

## The Ace Take

Yesterday proved the model knows when to trust its convictions. Five wins on a nine-game card keeps you in the rotation. Tomorrow's a coin flip game, but I'll take the home pitcher with his regular routine over the reliever-turned-starter experiment.

Trust your stuff, and we'll see you after first pitch.
